description: Only films whose replacement cost is strictly higher than 20.99 are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.

d.request: Only films with `replacement_cost` strictly greater than 20.99 (films at exactly 20.99 excluded) are used. For each `rating`, take the average `rental_duration` and the average of `rental_rate`/`replacement_cost`, ignoring NULLs. Then return one row with the average of those per-rating durations and the average of those per-rating ratios, unrounded.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_dur) AS avg_of_avg_rental_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_rate_to_cost_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_dur, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) t

b.request: Only films with `replacement_cost` strictly greater than 20.99 (films at exactly 20.99 excluded) are used. For each `rating`, take the average `rental_duration` and the average `rental_rate`/`replacement_cost` ratio, ignoring NULLs. Then return one row with the average of those per-rating duration averages and the average of those per-rating ratio averages, unrounded.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_dur) AS avg_of_avg_rental_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_rate_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_dur, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) t
b.raw: Only films with `replacement_cost` strictly greater than 20.99 (films at exactly 20.99 excluded) are used. For each `rating`, take the average `rental_duration` and the average `rental_rate`/`replacement_cost` ratio, ignoring NULLs. Then return one row with the average of those per-rating duration averages and the average of those per-rating ratio averages, unrounded.

c.request: For the pricier-to-replace films, with 20.99 as the `replacement_cost` cutoff, what are the average `rental_duration` and the average `rental_rate`-to-`replacement_cost` ratio for each `rating` (ignoring missing values)? Then give me one row with the average of those per-rating durations and the average of those per-rating ratios, in that order and unrounded. Only films whose replacement cost is strictly higher than 20.99 are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_dur) AS avg_of_avg_rental_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_dur, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 AND rating IS NOT NULL AND rental_duration IS NOT NULL AND rental_rate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating) t

a.request: Considering only films whose `replacement_cost` is more than 20.99, work out for each `rating` the average `rental_duration` and the average ratio of `rental_rate` to `replacement_cost` (ignoring missing values). Then return a single row with the average of those per-rating average durations and the average of those per-rating average ratios, in that order and unrounded.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_dur) AS avg_of_avg_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_dur, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) t
